messages:
anya: quick sync — we need a final list of runtime signals for the new per-1k token cost dashboard.
anya: goal: show raw cost, cache/batch savings, and a breakdown by routing policy + quota buckets.
sam: +1. can we pin the minimum fields? infra needs a stable schema to start exporting.
leo: here are what I think we need from runtime (short):
- model_variant (string)
- region (string)
- customer_tier (string)
- request_id (id)
- tokens_input (int)
- tokens_output (int)
- cache_hits (int)  # prefix/KV hits
- batch_size (int)
- kernel_ms (float)
- gpu_ms (float)
- fallback_reason (optional string)
- route_policy (string)  # e.g., lowcost/latency/pinned

maria: add: quota_bucket (string) — customers on shared vs reserved and rate-limited buckets need separate unit-econ.
ishaan: also export pricing_profile_id so we can map to per-token pricing (some customers have committed discounts).
sam: agree. we should version the schema: econ_v1. We'll lean on a lightweight proto for the telemetry event.
anya: can we show a tiny proto example in this thread? that helps infra + analytics align quickly.
leo: sure — rough proto (very small):
```proto
message EconEventV1 {
  string model_variant = 1;
  string region = 2;
  string customer_tier = 3;
  string pricing_profile_id = 4;
  int64 tokens_input = 5;
  int64 tokens_output = 6;
  int32 cache_hits = 7;
  int32 batch_size = 8;
  double gpu_ms = 9;
  string route_policy = 10;
  string quota_bucket = 11;
  string request_id = 12;
}
```
maria: looks good. callout: cache_hits needs to be consistent across prefetched prefixes. We used to have off-by-one differences between runtime and cache layer.
ishaan: noted. runtime will standardize: cache_hits = number of tokens served from KV cache for this request (0 if none).
anya: nice. next: telemetry join points. analytics wants both granular events (per request) and aggregates (hourly). How do we signal batching/non-batching?
leo: batch_size is the key. also include "batch_window_ms" if we want to analyze latency vs batch tradeoffs.
sam: and add a field for "is_streamed" boolean — streamed responses affect observed latency but not token accounting.
anya: for the dashboard calculations we need: total_tokens = tokens_input + tokens_output; cost_base = price_lookup(pricing_profile_id, model_variant) * total_tokens; cache_savings = cache_hits * price_lookup(...) ?? — rough idea.
maria: product asks for an easy breakdown: raw cost, cache savings, batching savings, network/infra overhead. We can approximate batching savings by comparing average per-token gpu_ms vs baseline single-token ms.
ishaan: for initial rollout, keep batching savings as a derived metric in analytics (don't require runtime to compute). runtime just emits gpu_ms and batch_size.
leo: routing policy nuance: when a request falls back from lowcost -> latency tier, we want metadata that shows attempted_policy and final_policy. add attempted_policy (string) optional.
anya: good call. also include "fallback_reason" already in proto.
sam: quotas: we need to tag events with quota_bucket + quota_limit and quota_remaining at the time of request, otherwise dash can't show near-quota behaviors. do we want those in every event? overhead cost is small (two ints).
maria: yes include quota_remaining (int) and quota_limit (int). helps for quota-aware routing views.
leo: updated proto suggestion: add quota_limit, quota_remaining, attempted_policy.
anya: OK — infra owners: can you confirm export cadence and retention? analytics wants raw events for 14 days and hourly aggregates for 13 months.
ishaan: we can stream raw events to events-pipeline (kafka) with a topic econ.events.v1. retention for raw = 14d. we will produce hourly rollups to econ.hourly.v1 with 13mo retention.
sam: routing: how do console rollouts control what routing policy is used? product expects a toggle in console with canary % and force-fallback. We need a route policy id that maps to both runtime behavior and UI names.
maria: UX note — show a small badge on dashboard rows that indicates when customers were on a canary routing policy. e.g., yellow dot + "canary 10%".
leo: implementationally: console writes config to control-plane; control-plane pushes policy_id + canary_percent to runtime. runtime attaches policy_id + attempted_policy + final_policy to events.
anya: perfect. now edge cases: what happens for composite calls (multiple model calls per user-facing request)? analytics wants to attribute per-user-visible request. we need a root_request_id and a per-call request_id.
ishaan: we can propagate root_request_id if product opts-in. default emit request_id only. adding root_request_id optional field won't hurt.
sam: final checklist before I close this:
- proto schema updated with quota_limit/quota_remaining/attempted_policy/root_request_id/batch_window_ms/is_streamed
- topic: econ.events.v1 produced by runtime, retention 14d
- hourly aggregator to econ.hourly.v1, retention 13mo, includes derived metrics: cost_base, cache_savings, batching_savings
- console: expose route policy canary config + show canary badges in dashboard rows
- analytics: mapping from pricing_profile_id -> price per token table owned by finance (need contact)

maria: finance contact is @sam-finance (I'll ping).
anya: who owns the schema PR? leo + ishaan collab. sam will draft analytics mapping and dashboard wireframes. I'll schedule a 30m sync tomorrow.
leo: i'll open a proto PR and attach a minimal example exporter in runtime.
ishaan: will add topic wiring + doc in infra-runbooks.
anya: thanks all. quick followups in thread please. :thumbsup:
dash-bot: NOTE: created ticket INF-6123 to track econ.events.v1 onboarding. assignees: leo, ishaan.
sam: pinging @sam-finance for pricing table.
maria: adding a short doc in /docs/dashboards/econ-signals.md once proto lands.
anya: end — small async items: leo send PR, ishaan wire topic, sam share pricing, maria wireframe.
